## Favorite Equation

In a social network, nodes represent actors (e.g., individuals), while edges represent interactions between them (e.g., sending messages/signals).

A Relational Event Model (REM) estimates the rate at which each possible sender-receiver pair interacts at a given time, based on previous interactions and specified characteristics.

The event rate is modeled as:

$$\log \lambda(s,r,t) = \sum_{p=1}^{P} \beta_p X_p(s,r,t)$$

and interpreted as a one-unit increase in a statistic ($X_p$) is associated with a relative increase or decrease in the event rate ($\lambda$), depending on the magnitude and direction of its coefficient ($\beta_p$), holding all other statistics constant.

Where:

- $\lambda(s,r,t)$: Instantaneous event rate between sender $s$ and receiver $r$ at time $t$.

- $X_p(s,r,t)$: Endogenous or exogenous network characteristic describing the $(s,r)$ pair at time $t$.

- $\beta_p$: Model coefficient indicating how statistic $p$ affects the log event rate.

- $P$: Total number of statistics included in the model.

Reference: [Meijernik-Bosman et al. 2022](https://journals.plos.org/plosone/article?id=10.1371/journal.pone.0272309)
